title: Audit query playground + sparklines + CSV proto
content:
Purpose
Quick proto/notes for an "audit query playground" UX that combines: freeform query composer, saved views, inline sparklines for actor/activity volume, and one-click CSV/NDJSON export. Goal is to support engineers and security reviewers to iterate on queries, spot-volume anomalies, and export filtered slices for incident investigation or compliance requests.

Why a playground (context)
- Current audit view is too rigid: fixed facets, hard to combine time windows, and slow to iterate.
- Security folks often ask for narrow slices (user X, service-account Y, path Z, time range) and want to export results to run local forensics.
- We also get repeated requests to correlate audit events with deployment rollouts and cost spikes — showing small sparklines next to filters helps triage.

Guiding principles
- Fast iteration: immediate preview of sample rows (first N), with continuable pagination.
- Lightweight analytics: small sparklines per filter or actor to indicate recent activity (30d/7d/24h).
- Export-first mindset: make CSV/NDJSON export explicit and auditable (who exported what + export filters retained in audit log).
- RBAC-aware: queries limited by viewer scope; anonymize or redact fields for roles without PI access.
- Save & share: ability to save query as a named view (team-scoped or org-scoped) and link to it.

Core screens / wireframe notes
1) Top bar: Query composer + quick presets
- Freeform composer: structured syntax (field:value) + natural language helper ("last 7 days for deploy events by service-account")
- Quick presets: last 24h / 7d / 30d, deploy-events, auth-failures, api-key-creation, service-account-rotation
- Pinned filters area: drag filters into pinned zone to keep them across views
- Timebox control: custom range + relative quick buttons (e.g., business hours filter)

2) Results panel (split view)
- Left: sample rows table (paginated, first 100 rows by default)
- Right: context panel with small widgets: sparklines, facet counts, top actors, geo map (optional)
- Each row action menu: link to full event JSON, "export row" and "open investigation" (pre-populates incident template)
- Columns: timestamp, actor, event_type, resource, outcome, request_id, duration_ms (if present)

3) Sparklines & mini-metrics
- Show mini 7d sparkline next to actor/facet name in the right panel and in the facet chips
- Hover shows tooltip (peak timestamp, count) and ability to click-to-filter on that timeslice
- Sparklines are computed from aggregated counts to avoid row-level compute cost

4) Export modal
- Options: CSV (flatten), NDJSON (full payload), Sample (first N rows), All (up to org quota)
- Include/exclude columns UI (checkbox list), with "Include raw payload" toggle
- Export is an auditable action: requires a reason (free text) for non-admins; reason stored in export audit log
- Progress UI: streaming download indicator + link to archived export in console artifacts when complete

5) Save view UX
- Save as team view or org view (org views require admin approval)
- Meta: name, description, owner, tags, default time range
- Sharing: generate link (resolves to a deep-linked query), optionally snapshot results for historical export
- Version: keep simple history of saved views (who changed it + small diff)

RBAC and privacy notes
- Users without "PI-access" role will see redacted_actor fields (hash or truncated) and no IP geolocation
- Export permission matrix: only roles with "audit:export" can run full exports; others limited to sample
- Service accounts used in queries: surface last-used timestamp and associated principal (if permitted)

Performance / backend considerations (engineering notes)
- Preview must use fast indices; avoid full scan for each change. Use precomputed time-series aggregates for sparklines.
- Export should trigger a background job if result set > 100k rows; return artifact link when ready.
- Rate limits: per-user export cap / day, and per-query complexity timeout (to avoid long-running queries affecting runtime)
- Consider using the existing metrics pipeline (observability infra) to compute sparklines to avoid coupling to event storage

Open questions / tradeoffs
- Syntax: strict structured only, or hybrid NL + structured? Hybrid is more friendly but harder to parse reliably.
- Snapshots vs live view for saved views: snapshotting ensures reproduceability for audits but costs storage.
- Column-level redaction policy: should this be role-configurable at org level? (ask legal/compliance)
- Export retention and access controls: how long do we keep generated exports? default 30 days?

Backlog (prioritized)
- M1: Query composer + instant preview + basic export (sample + CSV limited to 10k rows) + saved view (team-scope)
- M2: Sparklines (7d/30d) for top facets + facet chips with counts + export NDJSON + export job artifacts
- M3: RBAC redaction rules + admin approval workflow for org-scope saved views + export audit UI
- M4: Snapshot-on-save option + CSV schedule/export API + integration with incident playbooks

Notes / TODOs (author)
- TODO: sync with security on redaction defaults (Anya)
- TODO: Jira epic for background export job (Diego)
- TODO: UX mockup for composer autocomplete (Ravi)
- Quick research: find examples of "query playground" in other consoles (e.g., CloudTrail Insights, Datadog Log Explorer) — capture behavioral patterns.

Meeting points for next grooming session
- Bring engineering feasibility for sparklines (cost estimate)
- Present initial composer prototype (text or simple interactive) for feedback
- Confirm export compliance requirements with legal (retention & evidence chain)

Rough sketches (verbal, paste into Miro/figma later)
- Top: composer bar, right side quick preset chips
- Body split 60/40: left table, right context panel
- Each facet chip: label + small sparkline + count + overflow menu (convert to filter / pin / mute)
- Export modal is bottom-docked drawer with progress rail

Notes-to-self: keep saved views lightweight; avoid creating too many org views by default.

End of proto notes.
